correctness.rationale: The path–clique Cartesian metric equals |i-t| plus a binary color-mismatch term. For any two candidate vertices, equality of landmark distances forces a monotone integer difference f(t) with fixed parity. Color projection gives the sharp q-1 lower bound; at q>=4 simultaneous zero/odd offsets make all injections resolve, while q=3 needs either three colors or a two-color alternating pattern; q=2 forces same-color endpoints. The all-case necessity, sufficiency and counts are explicitly reconstructed in RESULT.md. A BFS/adjacency checker independently enumerated 72,202 independent candidate sets in 28 instances, all passing; this does not replace the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general projection lemma yields the q-1 lower bound but not the existence of independent resolving bases, which can fail for short L. The ordinary dimension equality cannot imply idim=q-1 at q=3, because in fact idim=3. Results for paths, cycles, and grids do not dominate this complete-clique factor family.

originality.rationale: The claim jointly classifies independent resolving feasibility, independent metric dimension and all minimum bases of P_L square K_q. The closest relevant prior theorems establish general independent resolving-number theory, ordinary metric dimension of the product, or independent metric dimension of grids and path–cycle products. None of the inspected full-text results states or implies the complete clique–path classification, including the exceptional K_3 penalty and basis multiplicities. Mathematical-record and literature searches returned no equivalent claim, subject to stated residual priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The 2021 Cartesian-product study motivates identifying when a product admits independent resolving landmarks. Here the entire path–clique family is classified by a sharp, variable-width existence threshold, with an exceptional q=3 penalty relative to the ordinary dimension and a full factorial/binomial count of all optimal configurations. This is a natural metric identification invariant not supplied by generic projections or one-number product bounds; the full labeled-basis classification is reproducible and structurally explained.
